# Chesed Brainstorm — Full 180-Second Manifestation

The Awtsmoos has no shortage of paths, while Awtsmoos.com must choose a vessel that keeps every one of 2,160 moments truthful, reproducible, and alive.

## Possible strategies
1. Run the exact proven sequential frame pump unchanged. Highest confidence, lowest new-code risk, longest runtime.
2. Use two independent hidden canvases and alternate even/odd frame indices. Could nearly halve render/JPEG wall time if the browser parallelizes canvas work.
3. Use four independent hidden canvases with modulo frame ownership. Higher throughput potential, higher CPU/memory contention.
4. Render sequentially but overlap only HTTP upload after each JPEG Blob is created. Network is already cheap, so expected gain is small.
5. Render sequentially and batch HTTP requests. Does not address dominant Canvas/JPEG cost.
6. Build an OffscreenCanvas worker pool. Potentially powerful but introduces a new browser-worker renderer boundary and much more verification risk.
7. Lower fps or resolution. Rejected because the proof contract is explicitly 640×360 at 12fps.
8. Change JPEG quality. Could reduce transfer, but transfer is not dominant and fidelity should remain stable.
9. Reuse short-proof encoded sections. Rejected because the full movie must render its entire canonical timeline, including later scenes and Teacher dialogue.
10. Pre-render scene backgrounds. Possible future optimization, but risks changing animation semantics.
11. Run sequential baseline now while other independent repo work proceeds in another browser target. Safe and truthful.
12. Benchmark a bounded multi-source pool on a small proof before committing the full film.

## Ideal architecture
A frame-pool abstraction owns N independent `MalchusCanonicalMovieJpegFrameSource` instances. Each lane receives immutable frame indices, renders exact `index/fps` time, produces a JPEG, uploads by exact index, and reports completion through one shared counter. The native server already supports out-of-order indexed files and finalizes only after exact cardinality, making bounded parallel staging semantically possible.
